newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LAWLESS SCORES 50 POINTS IN NATAL RAMPAGE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LAWLESS SCORES 50 POINTS IN NATAL RAMPAGE.

text.p: Natal fullback Gavin Lawless piled up 50 points to set a South African provincial points scoring record in his side's 75-43 victory over Otago in a Super 12 match on Saturday.
Lawless, who joined Natal in the off-season from Transvaal, ran in four tries and finished the day with a perfect goal kicking record, landing nine conversions and four penalties.
The brilliant individual effort surpassed the previous record of 48 points held jointly by De Wet Ras (1977), Jannie de Beer (1992) and Jaco Nel (1994).

Natal, beaten by Auckland in last year's Super 12 final, turned on a scorching display of running rugby to score nine tries. The New Zealand side, who came back strongly in the final quarter, ran in six of their own.
Both sides showed a willingness to spread the ball wide, even though the match was played in humid conditions with the temperature reaching 32 degrees Celsius.
Although the Natal side were without the services of injured Springbok Andre Joubert, and James Small and Steve Atherton who have left the club, they completely dominated the first half.
Natal raced in five tries to lead 41-17 at the break.
Lawless, who scored his first try late in the first half, collected three in the second, including two in the last seven minutes, to cap a remarkable performance.

Natal - Gavin Lawless; Dirkie Strydom, Jeremy Thomson, Joos Joubert, Cabous van der Westhuizen; Henry Honiball, Kevin Putt; Gary Teichmann (captain), Dieter Kriese (Wayne Fyvie 65), Walter Minnaar (Wayne Fyvie 52), Mark Andrews, John Slade (Waye Boardman 75), Adrian Garvey, John Allan (Danie van der Walt 74), Rob Kempson (Ollie le Roux 44).

Otago - Matthew Carrington; Jeff Wilson, Romi Ropati (Jason Wright 42), John Leslie, Manassa Bari; Tony Brown, Brett McCormack; Taine Randell (captain), Kupu Vanisi (Isotolo Maka 42), Lio Falaniko, Tiwini Hemi, Steve Gordon (Ace Tiatia 67), Kees Meeuws, Anton Oliver, Carl Hoeft (Mike Mika 74).
